clue.text: Music producer, fraud

definitions.meaning: a violin, an instrument that makes music, is informally called by this name
a swindle or scam, as in a tax dodge

explanation.surface: A record producer is exposed as a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a violin is a fiddle, and a fiddle is also a swindle or dishonest scheme.

clue.text: At the outset, football player finds agent

indicators.note: at the start of the word football, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: an actor plays a part on stage

explanation.surface: Right from the start, a footballer goes looking for someone to represent him.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a commercial agent who buys and sells on another's behalf; also something that acts to bring a result.

clue.text: Inspiration will bring one down

parts.note: inspiration here is breathing in, which happens when the muscle under the lungs contracts and moves downward

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' suggests a creative idea or a muse; read literally it is drawing breath, and the sheet of muscle beneath the lungs drops as you inhale.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed muscle under the lungs flattens and descends when you breathe in, so inhaling brings it down.

clue.text: More than one vegetable has a hole in it, we hear?

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a container with a hole in it leaks

explanation.surface: A puzzled cook finds a vegetable with a hole in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: these are onion-family vegetables with long white stems, more than one of them.

clue.text: A passage in plot carried off

indicators.note: the passage word sits inside the plot word

parts.note: a plot of garden ground, as in a flower bed
a duct is a channel or tube carrying air or fluid

explanation.surface: A secret passage in a conspiracy is used to spirit someone away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a conspiracy but is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kidnapped has been taken away by force, i.e. carried off.

clue.text: Routine to look at occupying basic accommodation, say

indicators.note: the reading word takes up residence inside the lodging abbreviation

parts.note: B and B, bed and breakfast, a simple guesthouse stay
to read a text is to look at it
to utter is to say aloud

explanation.surface: A guest reads while staying somewhere cheap and simple, then says something.
explanation.walkthrough: B AND B is the British short form of bed and breakfast, a small guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes everyday, routine work that forms the basic income of a business.

clue.text: United and City plan to play. That's remarkable

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: the letters are set loose to play about and land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Two football clubs, United and City, agree a plan to play each other — quite something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' sits as football language but signals the rearrangement of CITY PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not typical stands out from the norm, so it is noteworthy.

clue.text: I'm thankful to secure easy goal

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
to pin something is to fasten it in place

explanation.surface: A grateful striker scores a simple goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a close-range shot into an open net is the simplest kind of score.

clue.text: Peculiar bend in formal attire

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or odd, as in a dicky heart
to bow is to bend at the waist

explanation.surface: Someone bends awkwardly while dressed up for a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: DICKY is British slang for faulty or unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie, worn with a dinner jacket, is part of black-tie evening dress.

clue.text: What further explains what ballet term's doing?

definitions.meaning: a note sent with a job application or document to explain it
the two words ballet term, run together, hold the six letters of a written message inside them, so they are covering one

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful reading: the run of letters 'balLETTERm' wraps around LETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A note sent with an enclosed CV or document explains and introduces what accompanies it.

clue.text: Go with "Tea for Two", not half!

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea
per means for each, as in per person
half of two is one, so taking two and halving it gives one

explanation.surface: A cry that the song 'Tea for Two' is a great idea — 'not half!' meaning absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so'; here it means two halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is a companion who goes with someone, especially a young person, to supervise.

clue.text: Carbon on helmet something to discuss

indicators.note: in an across answer the carbon symbol goes after the helmet word, tacked on

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, a pith helmet
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Soot on a helmet becomes a talking point.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of conversation or debate.

clue.text: I say nothing to Elizabeth, ultimately

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: the final letters of the words to and Elizabeth are taken

explanation.surface: Someone tells Elizabeth nothing in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise or delight, like 'I say!' or 'my word!'.

clue.text: Go to invest very little?

definitions.meaning: go to the lavatory, a euphemism
to lay out a single small coin

explanation.walkthrough: The British euphemism for using a toilet comes from old public toilets that cost a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending a penny means visiting the loo, a British euphemism, and literally laying out one coin.

clue.text: Unfinished track, short feature that consists of slow movements

indicators.note: the tracking word lacks its end letter, so it is not finished

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow or track them

indicators.note: the facial feature is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A half-built racetrack and a stumpy bit of a design make up something slow-moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a noun, a racecourse; it is the verb, to tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese martial art is practised as a sequence of slow, flowing exercises.

clue.text: See eccentric king, perhaps?

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to court them
a card is an amusing odd character

explanation.surface: Visiting an oddball monarch, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a bishop's see or looking; here it is courting.
explanation.definitionFit: The king, like queen and jack, is one of the picture ranks in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Don't ask me to recall party with love

indicators.note: recall read as call back, so the party word comes back to front

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
and means together with
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to remember a party where love was in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is the usual British short form for the Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal refusal meaning 'it can't be done', as when declining a request.

clue.text: Noisome, vacant girl given makeover for new term

indicators.note: the letters are restyled into a new arrangement
the word girl is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: An unpleasant, empty-headed girl gets a makeover for the new school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given makeover' shuffles NOISOME with GL, which is 'girl' emptied by 'vacant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined word or expression not yet established in the language is a neologism.

clue.text: Display toilet while in Oxford, perhaps?

indicators.note: the toilet and while words go inside the footwear word

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced shoe
WC, water closet
as, meaning during the time that

explanation.surface: Showing off a toilet while visiting the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the city; it is a kind of lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass display case, or any setting that exhibits something to best advantage.

clue.text: Hat good on Spanish chap briefly adopting uniform

indicators.note: in an across answer the good letter goes after the rest
the shortened Spanish word takes in the uniform letter
the Spanish word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: hombre is Spanish for man
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smart hat looks fine on a Spanish fellow in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim, named after a German town.

clue.text: Additional English city

definitions.meaning: a ... is an extra fitted later
a large town in Greater Manchester, north-west England

explanation.walkthrough: It is a large town near Manchester, England; the clue calls it a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt-on addition is an extra component attached later, and Bolton is a Lancashire mill town.

clue.text: Fancy horse to steal race after one's been dropped

indicators.note: the horse takes the letter into itself, pocketing it

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse

indicators.note: the word race has its one dropped, leaving a single letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A fancied horse is to steal the race after another runner falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' minus ACE (one, as on a playing card) leaves just R.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is fancy and decorated, with frills and ruffles.

clue.text: Town, on-line, requested Wilts hotel to renovate old bar

indicators.note: renovate means to rebuild, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
estop is an old legal word meaning to bar or prevent

explanation.surface: A council plans to renovate an old bar in a Wiltshire hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilts is the short form of Wiltshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town on a railway line where trains halt only on request or signal.

clue.text: I was competitive with climber going up the wall?

definitions.text: with climber going up the wall?

parts.note: vied means competed

explanation.surface: Someone recalls competing with a rival rock climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' looks like a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for a building covered in ivy, a plant that clambers up walls.

clue.text: Dirge, primarily, in Ring Cycle

indicators.note: the dirge letter goes inside the ringing word

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word Dirge is used

explanation.surface: A mournful song features in Wagner's Ring Cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring Cycle' suggests Wagner's operas; 'Cycle' alone is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a bicycle is to push its pedals round with the feet.

clue.text: Blade is article in gold

indicators.note: the article sits inside the gold word

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A blade turns out to be a golden object.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of a rowing implement is its blade, and rowers call the whole thing a blade.

clue.text: Soul only partly evident in salesman, I'm afraid

indicators.note: the letters are only partly on show inside the words, so they are concealed there

explanation.surface: A salesman admits to having little soul.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner self or soul.

clue.text: Routine taking days, feeding papers into drawer

indicators.note: the paper-and-days group is fed in, put inside the next word
into confirms that the group goes inside the cash-drawer word

parts.note: a till is a cash drawer in a shop

indicators.note: the paper word takes in the days letter

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A clerk spends days feeding papers into a drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a tedious repetitive routine, from the walking mill once used as punishment.

clue.text: Layer of cells in men odder after surgery

indicators.note: the letters are reworked as if operated on

explanation.surface: Men are left odder after their operation, down to the cells.
explanation.definitionFit: In embryology the innermost germ layer of cells, which forms the gut lining.

clue.text: My fruit, via squeezes

indicators.note: the via word holds the fruit tightly inside it

parts.note: by means through or by way of
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone's fruit gets squeezed through something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive; it is the exclamation, as in 'my, my'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise, British, just as 'My!' or 'Goodness!' expresses astonishment.
